library(tidyverse)

# Load and Process Data

```{r function}
# --------------------------------------------------
# Function: process_air_quality()
#
# Purpose:
#   Read and clean one year of EPA air quality data.
#
# Arguments:
#   file_path = path to csv file
#   ozone_unit = desired ozone units ("ppm" or "ppb")
#
# Returns:
#   A cleaned tibble with one row per day
# --------------------------------------------------

process_air_quality <- function(file_path, ozone_unit = "ppm") {

  # Read csv file
  dat <- read_csv(file_path, show_col_types = FALSE)

  # Rename pollutant variables
  dat <- dat %>%
    rename(
      co = `Daily Max 8-hour CO Concentration`,
      pm25 = `Daily Mean PM2.5 Concentration`,
      ozone = `Daily Max 8-hour Ozone Concentration`
    )

  # Convert Date to Date format
  dat <- dat %>%
    mutate(Date = mdy(Date))

  # Replace negative pollutant values with 0
  pollutants <- c("co", "pm25", "ozone")

  for(var in pollutants){
    dat[[var]][dat[[var]] < 0] <- 0
  }

  # Average multiple measurements within a day
  dat <- dat %>%
    group_by(Date) %>%
    summarize(
      co = mean(co, na.rm = TRUE),
      pm25 = mean(pm25, na.rm = TRUE),
      ozone = mean(ozone, na.rm = TRUE),
      .groups = "drop"
    )

  # Convert ozone to ppb if requested
  if(ozone_unit == "ppb"){
    dat <- dat %>%
      mutate(ozone = ozone * 1000)
  }

  # Remove duplicate rows
  dat <- distinct(dat)

  return(dat)
}
```

# Process Each Year

```{r process-years}
aq18 <- process_air_quality("AQ_2018.csv")
aq19 <- process_air_quality("AQ_2019.csv")
aq20 <- process_air_quality("AQ_2020.csv")

air_quality <- bind_rows(aq18, aq19, aq20)

air_quality <- air_quality %>%
  mutate(
    year = year(Date),
    month = month(Date, label = TRUE, abbr = TRUE)
  )

head(air_quality)
```

# Tables

## 2018

```{r table-2018}
table_2018 <- aq18 %>%
  summarise(
    CO_Min = min(co, na.rm = TRUE),
    CO_Max = max(co, na.rm = TRUE),
    PM25_Min = min(pm25, na.rm = TRUE),
    PM25_Max = max(pm25, na.rm = TRUE),
    Ozone_Min = min(ozone, na.rm = TRUE),
    Ozone_Max = max(ozone, na.rm = TRUE)
  )

kable(round(table_2018, 3),
      caption = "2018 Daily Minimum and Maximum Pollutant Concentrations")
```

# Plot 1: CO and Ozone by Month

```{r plot1}
monthly_summary <- air_quality %>%
  pivot_longer(
    cols = c(co, ozone),
    names_to = "pollutant",
    values_to = "value"
  ) %>%
  group_by(month, pollutant) %>%
  summarise(
    mean = mean(value, na.rm = TRUE),
    sd = sd(value, na.rm = TRUE),
    n = sum(!is.na(value)),
    se = sd / sqrt(n),
    lower = mean - 1.96 * se,
    upper = mean + 1.96 * se,
    .groups = "drop"
  )

ggplot(monthly_summary,
       aes(x = month,
           y = mean,
           color = pollutant,
           group = pollutant)) +
  geom_point(size = 3) +
  geom_line() +
  geom_errorbar(aes(ymin = lower, ymax = upper),
                width = 0.2) +
  labs(
    title = "Monthly Average CO and Ozone Concentrations",
    x = "Month",
    y = "Concentration"
  ) +
  theme_minimal()
```

**Plot 1 Justification:** Ozone and CO are displayed together to compare seasonal trends, while confidence intervals show uncertainty in the monthly averages.

# Plot 2: PM2.5 by Month and Year

```{r plot2}
ggplot(air_quality,
       aes(x = month,
           y = pm25,
           color = factor(year),
           group = year)) +
  stat_summary(fun = mean, geom = "line", linewidth = 1) +
  stat_summary(fun = mean, geom = "point", size = 2) +
  labs(
    title = "Average PM2.5 Concentration by Month and Year",
    x = "Month",
    y = "PM2.5 Concentration",
    color = "Year"
  ) +
  theme_minimal()
```

**Plot 2 Justification:** A line plot makes it easy to compare month-to-month PM2.5 trends across years.

# Interpretation

- CO and ozone appear to show seasonal variation across the year.
- PM2.5 concentrations vary across months and years.
- Results for May-December should be interpreted carefully because 2020 data are only available through April.
